newsitem.title: GERMANY: Europe coffee trade sees some roaster price fixing.
newsitem.headline: Europe coffee trade sees some roaster price fixing.

text.p: Coffee traders in northern Europe said consumers limited their activities to price fixings amid ongoing concern over the nearby premium in New York.
London robusta futures were closed on Monday for a holiday and CSCE arabica futures edged higher early.
At 1415 GMT, the Sept/Dec spread in New York was at 9.85 cents compared with 9.70 cents at Friday's close and 10.30 on Thursday as September was down 1.45 at 130.80 cents/lb.
"Those in need of fixing September have a hard time at that level while others hope to stay out of the market until September goes off the board," one trader said.
"Levels of cover in the industry are debatable, there are some gaps, but consumers want to give the impression the situation is under control to get September out of the way."
There were also fears the Sept/Dec switch could be rolled forward into Dec/March, where the gap is currently just 6.30.
Although the open interest in New York is declining, it equals 500,000 bags of coffee, with Exchange warehouses only holding just under 35,000 bags.
"It could become very uncomfortable for the shorts," another trader said.
In the outright market, Colombian differentials were still at 20 cents over futures and Brazil differentials rose as exporters hiked prices in firm domestic markets.
Fob Bremen Brazils were at $124 per 50 kg and Colombians were at $153 for Oct/Nov shipment as traders reported some Colombian and Central American sales.
Buying was subdued as the level of roastings contracted in the European summer holiday period.
Physical robusta markes were well supplied by Indonesian and Ugandan material at competitive rates.
